prerequisites: Basic knowledge of chemistry and physics, level B1.

learning_outcomes.text: The student is familiar with the analytical process ranging from sample preparation, the execution of the measurement, and the processing of the measurement results.

The student knows the basic principles of standard and advanced techniques for the qualitative and/or quantitative analysis of industrially relevant samples (e.g., determining toxic components in the context of an environmental analysis, determining the purity of a final product, measuring hazardous substances in ambient air in the context of safety).
The student knows the possibilities and limitations of various techniques.
The student knows a number of common techniques applied in process analytical chemistry.
The student can make a motivated choice between techniques for a case study.
The student has acquired laboratory skills to work accurately, reproducibly, and safely.
The student has acquired laboratory skills for a set of analytical techniques.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: sample preparation, processing of results
Titrations: precipitation titrations, acid-base titrations, redox titrations, and complexometric titrations
Electroanalysis: introduction of basic principle, potentiometric measurement techniques (e.g., pH measurement)
Spectrometry: introduction of basic concepts and instrument, atomic spectrometry (e.g., atomic absorption spectrometry), and molecular spectrometry (e.g., infrared spectrometry)
Chromatography: introduction of basic concepts, gas chromatography, and liquid chromatography
Mass spectrometry: principle, atomic mass spectrometry, molecular mass spectrometry
Process analytical chemistry: sensors for inline and online detection in industrial processes

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period
Practicals and a subset of exercise sessions (participation, safe lab practices, results, reporting)

assessment_rules: The written exam accounts for 15 out of 20 points. Practicals and exercise sessions contribute 5 out of 20 points, based on mandatory attendance, application of good and safe lab practices, results, and reporting. During the resit, only the written exam is repeated, retaining the score from the practicals and exercise sessions.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
